item.title: Popular food could boost heart health, but the amount you need to eat may surprise you
item.description: A major meta-analysis of 87 trials reveals that 60 to 100 grams of whole grains daily may lower cholesterol, blood pressure and blood sugar levels.
item.content:encoded:
A bowl of oatmeal, a sandwich on whole-grain bread and a side of brown rice may do more for your heart and overall health than you think, according to a new study.

Eating four to six servings of whole grains each day may offer the greatest benefits for heart health, lowering body weight, cholesterol, blood sugar and blood pressure, a large meta-analysis published in the European Heart Journal found.

The analysis reviewed data from 87 randomized trials involving more than 6,500 people across Asia, Europe, the United States, Canada, Australia and Brazil. 

MAN SAYS MEAT-ONLY 'LION DIET' CLEARED PSORIASIS COVERING 90% OF HIS BODY, ENDED DECADES OF DEPRESSION

It found that many of the greatest benefits occurred when people ate about 60 to 100 grams of whole grains daily — about what you would get from a bowl of oatmeal, two slices of whole-grain bread and a serving of brown rice, according to the researchers.

"This is the largest and most comprehensive meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials on whole-grain intake and cardiovascular risk factors," lead author Helda Tutunchi, of Tabriz University of Medical Sciences in Iran, said in a statement.

People who consumed more whole grains had lower body weight, waist circumference, blood pressure, total cholesterol, LDL ("bad") cholesterol, triglycerides, blood glucose and levels of interleukin-6, an inflammatory marker, the study also found.

One key finding, Tutunchi noted, was that whole grains appeared to boost heart health through "several modest improvements acting together, rather than through one large effect on a single factor."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The researchers cautioned, however, that most of the studies they looked at were short and did not measure heart attacks or strokes directly. Longer-term research is still needed, they said.

Four to six servings of whole grains is more than the two to four servings the current Dietary Guidelines for Americans recommend — and many Americans don't even hit that, said Lauren Manaker, a South Carolina-based registered dietitian nutritionist.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"Going from zero to six is a lot," Manaker, who wasn't involved in the study, told Fox News Digital. "My recommendation is to start slow. Two servings is better than zero servings."

Simple swaps can include starting the day with oatmeal or overnight oats, or replacing refined grains with whole-grain sides such as sorghum or brown rice, she said.

Consumers should also be careful not to assume every brown-colored loaf at the supermarket is whole grain, Manaker added.

"We want to look at the ingredient list and make sure one of the first ingredients is a whole grain," she said. "We also want to look at the nutrition panel and make sure there's some fiber in there."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Whole grains contain all three parts of the grain kernel — the bran, germ and endosperm — rather than having some parts removed during processing, the researchers noted.

While researchers say more studies are needed, they concluded that increasing whole-grain intake is "a relatively simple, accessible and affordable dietary strategy" that can complement other heart-healthy habits.

In an editorial that accompanied the report, Cecilie Kyro of the Danish Cancer Institute in Copenhagen and her colleagues encouraged policies that make minimally processed whole-grain staples accessible, affordable and culturally acceptable while also "avoiding a drift towards ultra-processed products."

Fox News Digital reached out to the study's authors for comment.

item.description: Julius Hunter allegedly lured a teen to a fake $300 babysitting job on Craigslist before a hours-long sexual assault at a Clarkston apartment.
item.content:encoded:
Georgia investigators are searching for potential victims of a convicted Florida sex offender after DNA linked him to three sexual assault cases involving women allegedly lured through Craigslist job ads.

Julius Hunter, 42, faces rape, aggravated sodomy and kidnapping charges in Georgia in connection with a 2016 attack on a 19-year-old teen at a Clarkston apartment complex. A DeKalb County grand jury indicted him on Aug. 11.

Before his Georgia arrest, Hunter pleaded no contest in an unrelated 2021 Florida sexual battery case involving his former girlfriend. Investigators are now examining what they believe is a broader pattern of sexual assaults.

He has not been charged in either case. Rogers said investigators have been unable to reconnect with the two women.

The 19-year-old thought she was heading to a $300 overnight babysitting job when Hunter arranged a ride-share to an apartment near 700 Jolly Avenue on July 27, 2016, according to the DeKalb County District Attorney’s Office.

When she arrived, there were no children — only Hunter and another man, authorities said.

She attempted to leave, but Hunter allegedly stopped her and sexually assaulted her over several hours before releasing her the following day.

Rogers told Fox News Digital that investigators have not identified the second man inside the apartment and continue to seek information about him. He has not been charged.

The Clarkston case remained unsolved for years after the Georgia Bureau of Investigation developed a male DNA profile from the 19-year-old’s sexual assault kit. The profile was entered into the Combined DNA Index System (CODIS) but, at the time, did not match anyone in the national database.

Authorities arrested Hunter in Fort Lauderdale on Aug. 13, two days after the DeKalb County grand jury indicted him. He was extradited to Georgia and booked into the DeKalb County Jail on Aug. 20.

item.title: Rob Gronkowski says Caleb Williams' viral injury reaction was about 'passion' – not pain
item.description: Rob Gronkowski said Caleb Williams' viral hamstring injury reaction was driven by "passion," instead of the pain, drawing on his own 11-year NFL career.
item.content:encoded:
Caleb Williams’ reaction to his injury during the Chicago Bears’ Week 2 went viral after fans learned it wasn’t as bad as initially thought.

Fans began to rip Williams for how he treated his hamstring injury in the moment, as to Bears staffers helped him off the wet Soldier Field grass as his leg dragged on the turf. Then, he had a towel over his head on a cart to the locker room before taking it off and throwing up his fist to the sold-out crowd of Bears fans.

But when it came out that Williams would be week-to-week, instead of being lost for the season as his reaction seemed to indicate, he received backlash on social media from those who believed he exaggerated.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

For legendary NFL tight end Rob Gronkowski, he believes Williams’ "passion" was the reason for his reaction in the moment.

"Here’s the thing is that he’s never really been injured before from what I believe, so he doesn’t know truly what an injury is," Gronkowski told OutKick at a New York City event for his partnership with Bounty. "And he was riding on a high. He had a great game Week 1, he was ready to play all year going into this season. I feel like it was more about passion that he showed than being hurt with the injury – that’s the thing."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

From "Gronk’s" point of view, he also believed Williams was dealing with a severe injury, perhaps a Grade 3 hamstring strain based on the way he pulled up.

"If looked like it was a Grade 3 [strain], and Grade 3 I understand you’re like, ‘Oh my God.’ That one would hurt. You’re going to be pissed, you’re going to be sad, and you know it’s blown out," he added.

However, for someone who played through multiple injuries throughout his 11-year career in the league, Gronkowski knows the difference between a Grade 3, that would leave you out for weeks, and a week-to-week injury in the moment.

"If he’s week-to-week, it wasn’t the pain because I’ve had injuries. That’s not that much pain the way he went," Gronkowski explained. "But I would say he had so much passion going into the season, going into the game that. From my view and my opinion is that he was more hurt because he wasn’t sure how long of an injury that was and he wanted to be out there. He was just disappointed in that aspect."

While the Bears haven’t officially ruled out Williams for Week 3, head coach Ben Johnson said he considers his franchise quarterback to be week-to-week as they evaluate the injury moving forward. Williams’ backup, though, might not be available against the Philadelphia Eagles in Brazil, as Tyson Bagent is in concussion protocol.

He did, however, participate in practice on Saturday, so there is hope that Bagent will suit up and lead the offense in Week 3.

If Bagent can't go, that would leave Case Keenum, the journeyman third-string quarterback, to potentially be starting for Chicago in the primetime matchup on "Monday Night Football."

item.title: College football week 4 contenders, pretenders: Texas survives, Michigan's karma and coaches are sweating
item.description: Iowa stunned Michigan on a last-second touchdown, and LSU's Lane Kiffin sent Texas A&M fans into panic mode on a wild college football Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
KNOXVILLE, TN - It only took four weeks of action to immerse ourselves in the madness of college football, with upsets and teams already up against the ropes heading into the month of October.

Are schools already looking to make changes at the head coaching position? Sure, and some leaders might end up making the decision pretty easy for their bosses.

But what we witnessed on Saturday will go down as one of the wildest weekends of this early season, and there will be ramifications.

ARCH MANNING REVELS IN CIGAR SMOKE: TEXAS LEAVES NEYLAND WITH WIN—AND A WARNING FOR COLLEGE FOOTBALL

Heck, Texas led Tennessee by ten points late in the fourth quarter, but had to withstand a last minute drive by the Vols to get out of Knoxville with the win. There wasn’t even a touchdown pass thrown by Arch Manning on Saturday, but the defense ended up with over ten sacks on Vols quarterback Faizon Brandon, in what felt like a Will Muschamp defensive revival.

We're only getting started on this wild weekend in college football.

Oregon lost quarterback Dante Moore to a head injury in the first half, thanks to a dirty hit. But, that did not end their hopes of beating USC. Two weeks after losing to Oklahoma State, the Ducks rolled into Southern Cal and once again left Trojan fans wondering when Lincoln Riley was going to win a few meaningful games.

We don't know when Moore will return, but backup Dylan Raiola took the reigns on Saturday night and never looked back. Throwing for over 280 yards against USC, this might be the start of Raiola's redemption tour, at least until Dante Moore returns.

But, a massive 41-27 win for the Ducks have put their season back on track, while USC fans are left wondering what else Lincoln Riley feels like putting them through.

Who would of thought before the season started that Oklahoma would already be regretting that contract extension for Brent Venables. But just four games into the 2026 season, the Sooners have a major problem on their hands, thanks in part to the 41-13 drumming by the Georgia Bulldogs on Saturday afternoon in Athens.

Oh, and if you were wondering whether Ole Miss was walking into a trap this week in Gainesville after defeating LSU last weekend, I think that would be disrespecting what Jon Sumrall is doing with the Florida Gators.

A 52-28 loss on the road brought the Rebels back down to reality, with Pete Golding having to regroup his team this week after a rollercoaster two-week stretch. But make no mistake about it, the Florida Gators look nothing like the team we witnessed during the Billy Napier era.

FLORIDA DROPS IMPRESSIVE OFFENSIVE PERFORMANCE TO PULL OFF MASSIVE WIN OVER NO. 4 OLE MISS

And, speaking of teams we thought could get things back on track in 2026, South Carolina has itself a major problem moving forward under head coach Shane Beamer. Not only were they beaten 49-18 by Alabama, the Gamecocks feel like a rudderless ship, with such high expectations for quarterback LaNorris Sellers before the season began.

Now? The Gamecocks lost their seventh-straight SEC game, and it doesn’t look any better moving forward.

Well, this is only going to make things worse in Columbia for Beamer, who had spent a good chunk of money to keep a number of stars from hitting the portal, like Dylan Stewart.

Is Kamario Taylor going to end up being the catalyst that brings Mississippi State back to college football relevance? Well, he already has, and looks darn good in the process.

The 24th ranked Bulldogs defeated No. 19 Missouri, winning their first ranked game in over a decade, with Taylor passing for over 350 yards on the night.

Look out, Alabama. The Bulldogs are waiting next week in Starkville. \

Yes, you read that right.

An Iowa Hawkeyes touchdown with only one second left on the clock left Michigan fans stunned, probably the same way Western Michigan fans felt during the week-one controversy that allowed the Wolverines to escape with a win.

Three weeks later, it was Kirk Ferentz who delivered the karma like a Taylor Swift single, which had college football fans outside of the state chuckling I'd imagine.

No, this looks nothing like a team that should be paying its quarterback Bryce Underwood over $3 million per season. In reality, this feels like a squad headed for a December bowl game, and nowhere near the Big Ten championship. At this point, maybe it would be wise for Michigan fans to start preparing for the Ohio State game to end the season, and not get their hopes up every weekend.

That win against Oklahoma also looks even worse by the week.

So, you thought Lane Kiffin would just go quiet into the night after losing to his former team last week in Oxford?

Umm, no.

Not only did LSU take out their frustration on Texas A&M, but they made it look easy in the 38-6 win. Sam Leavitt carved up the Aggies secondary, while Kiffin found himself running down the sidelines celebrating a fourth-down trick play that turned into a touchdown.

Simply put, the Tigers made Mike Elko's squad look like a mediocre SEC team without much hope moving forward. We should probably go ahead and count the Aggies out of making the College Football Playoff, while LSU looks to have gotten the 'Lane Train' back on the tracks in Baton Rouge.

Can someone explain to me how Louisville could lose at home to Wake Forest 30-27, with this squad battling for 'surprise' team of the season out of the ACC?

Well, that went up in smoke inside their own stadium.

Oh, and how could we not mention the job Luke Fickell did on Saturday, leading his Wisconsin Badgers into Happy Valley and leaving with the 24-20 win that left folks in State College shocked. People forget that Fickell didn’t just wake up and turn into a bad coach. He just hasn’t had the necessary resources in Madison.

He still might not have everything he needs to rebuild the Wisconsin football team, but they darn sure made Penn State pay for potentially looking past the Badgers.

Week four of the college football season delivered, which will setup a wild start to the month of October.

Expect anything less?

item.title: UK police arrest 'explosive' suspects near US airbase, key to Iran war
item.description: Multiple suspects were arrested under the Explosives Act near RAF Fairford, prompting evacuations as explosive ordnance disposal teams examined vehicles.
item.content:encoded:
U.K. police say they arrested multiple suspects for offenses under the "Explosives Act" near a U.S. airbase in southwest England on Sunday.

Gloucestershire Police say the arrests took place just two miles from RAF Fairford, which hosts U.S. Air Force assets. The U.S. has recently used the base in operations relating to the war in IRan.

"A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident," Gloucestershire Police said in a statement. "It follows the arrest of several men on suspicion of offenses under the explosives act."

ANDY BURNHAM TAKES OVER AS UK PRIME MINISTER, CALLS FOR 'NEW POLITICAL MODEL'

"The Army's specialist explosive ordnance disposal team are currently examining a number of vehicles," police added.

Authorities did not name the suspects or detail exactly how many were arrested.

British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting wrote on X that the situation is "being dealt with."

UK PINS STRING OF ANTISEMITIC ATTACKS ON IRAN-LINKED GROUP, BANS IRGC

"The Prime Minister is being kept updated on the incident in Gloucestershire," The UK Defense Ministry said in another statement.

"We are grateful to the emergency services, who have acted quickly to detain several suspects and put measures in place to keep the community safe," the statement continued.

"It would be inappropriate to comment further whilst investigations are ongoing," it added.

WATER CYBERATTACK HITS AT LEAST 7 STATES

The incident comes roughly a month after Iran-linked hackers were suspected of forcing a small British power generator offline for several days this summer.

The British shutdown came weeks after hackers struck more than 30 community water systems in Minnesota, accessing technology used to remotely monitor and control pumps and other equipment. Minnesota officials have not publicly attributed the attacks. Several news outlets, citing U.S. officials and a leaked industry threat-sharing memo, reported that Iran was the likely culprit.

Federal agencies have also warned that Iranian-affiliated actors have targeted similar industrial devices across water, energy and government sectors, seeking access to the software used to control them. That activity has already caused operational disruptions and financial losses.

item.title: Knicks star Jalen Brunson shows some solid comedy chops in as 'SNL' season opening host
item.description: Jalen Brunson brought his Knicks teammates Josh Hart, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby, and Karl-Anthony Towns along for his "SNL" hosting monologue.
item.content:encoded:
"Saturday Night Live" got its 52nd season underway on Saturday night (duh), and the iconic New York City-based show went with a perfect host in New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson.

The NBA Finals MVP led the team to its first championship in decades, which makes him Big Apple royalty and a natural choice to host alongside musical guest KATSEYE (who had never heard of, but is apparently massively popular).

But athletes are a mixed bag when getting thrown on "SNL." Some turnouts have some comedy chops, while others are proven to have teh acting ability of a traffic cone.

KNICKS BEAT SPURS IN GAME 5 TO WIN FIRST NBA CHAMPIONSHIP SINCE 1973, ENDING 53-YEAR DROUGHT

So what was the case for Brunson?

Well, the first big hurdle was the monologue (after the requisite Trump-centric cold open), which I would argue is probably the hardest part of the gig for someone who isn't a regular performer.

Brunson did well, but it helped that he brought back up in the form of teammates Josh Hart, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby, and Karl-Anthony Towns.

Brunson also did a solid job in his first crack at a sketch in which he played a guy in the office who simply can't accept that he failed to shoot a wrapper into the trash from across the office.

Of course, there was plenty of basketball, and one of the best examples was a funny pre-taped sketch parodying "High School Musical."

The NBA star also had a role in a great "Shark Tank" parody about two entrepreneurs trying to get backing for a pair of glasses that sound an alarm any time the wearer looks at a woman's breasts. It was exactly the kind of weird sketch that always gets a laugh and often ends up being hilarious.

All in all, I think it's pretty safe to say that Brunson will easily go down as one of the better athletes to ever get the hosting gig. Maybe not on the level of Peyton Manning (who, for my money, is the best athlete host of all time), but certainly held his own.

Hey, maybe if the Knicks can go back-to-back, they'll bring him in again.

item.title: Legendary agent warns NFL teams about making key quarterback mistake that could derail season
item.description: Leigh Steinberg warned NFL teams keeping only two quarterbacks are jeopardizing their Super Bowl hopes as five starting QBs go down before Week 3.
item.content:encoded:
Amid a rash of quarterback injuries, legendary sports agent Leigh Steinberg thinks NFL teams that don’t have multiple backup options are putting their seasons and Super Bowl hopes in jeopardy.

Going into Week 3, five starting quarterbacks have already been injured, with New York Giants star Jaxson Dart out for the regular season. With the rash of injuries at the most important position in sports, Steinberg said it’s paramount that teams have multiple options.

"It's a real problem, which is why I always think that teams that don't keep three quarterbacks are making a mistake, because the likelihood is that the starting quarterback will be hurt at some point," Steinberg told OutKick in a recent interview.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The famed agent said that teams that have only two quarterbacks on the roster, like the Giants did with Dart and backup Jameis Winston, leave themselves exposed. If Winston had gotten hurt after Dart did on Monday night, the Giants would not have had another quarterback on the active roster and would have been in further trouble.

Now that Dart is hurt, the Giants are left scrambling to find a quality option behind Winston in the event the former Florida State star goes down while replacing Dart.

Steinberg noted that with the salary cap, it’s harder for teams to invest heavily in the backup quarterback position because starting quarterback salaries are ballooning. While it may be difficult to have multiple quality backups, Steinberg warned that teams that don’t have them leave themselves in a dangerous position.

"You have bigger, stronger defensive players on the line who can inflict all sorts of harm on the quarterback. The position starts with that player, so all the action coalesces around him, and there's just more opportunity to get hit and hurt," Steinberg said.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Despite rules that have been put in place to keep quarterbacks healthy, most notably in 2018 when the NFL restricted defenders from landing on quarterbacks with their full body weight, Steinberg said quarterbacks are vulnerable by the nature of the position.

Steinberg also noted that while an injury to a franchise quarterback is devastating to a team’s season, it’s also detrimental to the NFL. He noted how quarterbacks have become like movie stars in American culture and are the sport’s highest-profile celebrities, and injuries to them could cause viewership to decline.

However, Steinberg said that as much as the NFL has tried to protect quarterbacks with more "vigor," fans don’t notice the added measures because quarterbacks are still getting hurt.

"I want you to remember that every time they put in more protective rules and procedures. There's a hue and cry from football purists that they're taking the toughness out of the game," Steinberg said.

"I'm all for the most vigorous protections while retaining the competitive aspect of the game."

Steinberg, who was inducted into the California Sports Hall of Fame in 2017, has had many high-profile clients throughout his impressive career. Across football and baseball, Steinberg’s clients include Steve Bartkowski, Steve Young, Troy Aikman, Warren Moon, Bruce Smith, Thurman Thomas, Kordell Stewart, Jeff George, Ben Roethlisberger, Myron Rolle, Matt Leinart, Mark Brunell, Ricky Williams, Howie Long, Eric Karros and Dusty Baker, among others.

item.title: Iran ‘miscalculating’ by betting on midterms after 3-hour talks, Trump officials warn
item.description: President Donald Trump says Iran is waiting on midterm elections to cut a deal, but Marco Rubio warns Tehran misreads U.S. presidential powers.
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK — Trump officials say Iran is miscalculating if it believes rising prices and the midterm elections will weaken President Donald Trump's hand in negotiations to end the nearly seven-month conflict.

The administration is projecting confidence that mounting economic pressure will push Tehran toward a deal, even after three hours of talks this week ended without an announced breakthrough.

"The president holds all of the cards here," State Department principal deputy spokesperson Tommy Pigott told Fox News Digital in an on-camera interview on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly.

Americans, meanwhile, are facing a mounting cost at home. The national average for regular gasoline reached $4.49 per gallon Friday, according to AAA, up from $3.16 a year ago. AAA said volatility in the Strait of Hormuz and high crude oil prices have driven the national average to its highest level ever recorded for this time of year.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio acknowledged those costs Wednesday while arguing that allowing Iran to eventually obtain a nuclear weapon would carry a far greater price.

THE TOP MOMENTS FROM IRAN PRESIDENT’S TENSE VISIT TO US SOIL AS WAR RAGES

"It comes at a price and at a cost, there's no doubt about it," Rubio told reporters. "But the cost of not doing something about it is substantially higher, especially for future generations."

Trump himself laid out the stakes in stark terms during his address to the U.N. General Assembly Tuesday, presenting Tehran with a choice between reaching a deal that would allow Iran to rebuild or facing potentially devastating further U.S. action.

"Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?" Trump said. "Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?"

But Trump predicted Tehran would ultimately choose a deal, arguing that Iranian leaders are waiting to see whether the November midterm elections weaken his position.

"They're waiting to see how I do in the midterm election," Trump said. "What they don't realize is that I'm not running."

"I gave absolutely no credence and will not give credence to the election when it comes to Iran," Trump added. "It doesn't even enter my mind."

A U.S. official told Fox News Digital Friday that discussions through mediators remained "positive and constructive," but said the administration was in no hurry to reach an agreement.

"The United States is in a very strong position with control of the Strait of Hormuz, so we are not in a rush," the official said, adding that nearly 40 million barrels of oil had transited the strait over the previous 48 hours. The official predicted oil and gas prices would fall back to pre-conflict levels as the U.S. continues to maintain control of the strait.

Trump said U.S. officials held a "very good" three-hour meeting with Iranian officials Tuesday as part of a renewed diplomatic push to end the conflict. But Rubio cautioned Wednesday against characterizing the talks as a "major breakthrough," saying they were largely a continuation of previous conversations.

"I think it was significant that at least there was a conversation," Rubio said.

Rubio also said the administration would make public any "good outcomes or things to announce jointly" stemming from its diplomatic engagements. No such announcement immediately followed the Iran meeting.

Iran has since put forward a proposal of its own. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran presented U.S. mediators with a seven-day plan this week that would restore passage through the Strait of Hormuz at the end of the seven days if certain conditions are met, followed by renewed negotiations toward a broader agreement.

The proposal draws from the memorandum of understanding Trump and Iran reached in June. A mediator told CBS News the latest discussions were positive but remained in their early stages.

The stakes in Hormuz remain high. Commercial traffic through the critical oil chokepoint has been sharply disrupted during the conflict, although U.S. officials say the amount of oil moving through the strait is increasing.

TRUMP BETS ECONOMIC PRESSURE CAN SQUEEZE IRAN AS REGIME’S OWN FAILURES DEEPEN THE PAIN

"The diplomatic door is always open. The president is a deal maker," Pigott said. "But he's going to see the fundamental principle that they cannot have a nuclear weapon accomplished one way or another."

Pigott pointed to growing oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz and the economic pressure Washington has imposed on Tehran as evidence that the balance remains in Trump's favor.

"We are seeing oil move [through] the Strait of Hormuz, increasing every single day," Pigott said. "We're seeing the devastating effects on the Iranian regime from economic [actions]. Hundreds of millions of dollars are being denied to the regime through this blockade that we're seeing."

Rubio offered a similar assessment Wednesday when asked about Trump's assertion that Iran may be waiting for the outcome of the midterm elections before making a deal.

"I think the Iranians misread our system," Rubio said. "I think the Iranians are under this illusion that Democrats are going to win in November, and the president will no longer be able to do things against them."

Rubio said Congress remains an important branch of government but argued Tehran misunderstands the limits of congressional power over sanctions and military action.

"The president has extraordinary powers. Every president does," Rubio said. "He's the commander in chief, both constitutional and otherwise, to be able to carry out those functions."

"So I think that the Iranians are fundamentally misreading our political system," Rubio continued.

The administration is also confronting threats to energy infrastructure elsewhere in the region. Iran-backed Houthi rebels have targeted Saudi Arabia as the conflict has expanded, adding another source of uncertainty for global energy markets.

Rubio said Wednesday that the restart of a Saudi pipeline following attacks was "critical for their economy" and "critical for the global economy." He said energy infrastructure had been targeted by the Houthis as well as Shiite militias in Iraq that the U.S. says are backed by Iran.

"Every time you guys ask me a question about the Middle East, it goes back to someone who's supported by Iran," Rubio said.

Rubio said the U.S. would continue honoring its defense commitments to Saudi Arabia while declining to discuss what additional military options Trump could consider.

"They are a strategic defense partner," Rubio said. "The U.S. made commitments to them. We will live up to those commitments. We are living up to those commitments now."

item.title: Fake ChatGPT billing emails can steal your login
item.description: A phishing campaign impersonating OpenAI uses fake ChatGPT billing emails with a convincing login page to steal credentials and payment details.
item.content:encoded:
If you pay for ChatGPT, an email saying there is a problem with your subscription could easily get your attention. Maybe your card expired. Maybe the payment failed. Either way, you probably want to fix it before anything happens to your account. Cybercriminals are counting on that reaction.

Security researchers at Cofense uncovered a phishing campaign that impersonates OpenAI and ChatGPT. The fake email looks like a routine subscription notice. However, the button inside can lead to a convincing copy of the ChatGPT login page. Cofense says the campaign targets account credentials and payment information.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Get Better Healthcare With AI replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Get Better Healthcare With AI , has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay now at CyberGuyLive.com

SCAMMERS KNOW THE BEST TIME TO TEXT YOU

The scam starts with an email that looks polished enough to make you pause. According to the Cofense Phishing Defense Center, it uses the real ChatGPT logo and claims your subscription payment needs attention. Then comes the pressure. The message prominently displays "Subscription Payment Required." It also warns that you have 48 hours to act. A large "Update Payment Information" button gives you an obvious way to supposedly fix the problem. Finally, the message signs off as "The OpenAI Team." If you are checking email between meetings or quickly scrolling on your phone, all of that can feel believable. Cofense says the attackers combine familiar images, bold wording and urgency to push people into acting quickly.

The sender's email address is one of the biggest red flags. Cofense found that the phishing message came from support@9527db6e1a[.]nxcli[.]io. That domain has nothing to do with OpenAI. OpenAI currently lists several domains that it uses for legitimate customer emails. They include @openai.com, @mail.openai.com and @email.openai.com, along with other official OpenAI domains used for specific communications. That makes the full sender address worth checking. Do not rely on the name that appears in your inbox. A scammer can make the display name look reassuring while using a completely unrelated address behind it.

FAKE CHROME UPDATE SCAM COULD INFECT YOUR COMPUTER

The button inside this phishing email adds another layer of deception. Cofense found that clicking "Update Payment Information" first sent users through a Google API redirect. The link then forwarded them to the attacker's malicious site. That can make a suspicious link look more convincing at first glance because Google appears along the way. We have seen criminals abuse trusted services in similar attacks before. CyberGuy previously covered how hackers used legitimate Google Cloud tools to send phishing messages that looked like authentic Google notifications. So, seeing Google somewhere in a link does not tell you where you will eventually land. On a computer, hovering over a button can sometimes reveal the destination before you click. Still, redirects can make that check less useful. The safer option is to skip the email link entirely.

Once someone clicks through, the scam gets harder to spot. Cofense says the phishing page closely copies the ChatGPT login experience, complete with familiar logos, text and icons. However, the domain in the browser does not match the legitimate ChatGPT login domain identified by Cofense. If a victim enters login information, the fake site captures it and sends it to the attacker. The page then sends the victim to an error screen, which could easily look like a temporary login problem. By then, the attacker may already have the credentials. That is why it is worth checking the address bar before you enter a password. Scammers can copy the look of a login page. They cannot make an unrelated domain belong to OpenAI.

We reached out to OpenAI for comment but did not hear back before our deadline.

If an email says there is a payment problem, skip the button. Go directly to ChatGPT.com or open the official app and sign in yourself. For web subscriptions, OpenAI says to check Settings → Billing . Some accounts may show Settings → Account → Payment → Manage instead. If you subscribed through Apple or Google Play, manage your subscription through that store.

Expand the sender information and look at the actual email address. In this campaign, the sender used an nxcli.io domain. OpenAI publishes the domains it uses for legitimate communications, which gives you something concrete to compare against.

Check the browser address bar before entering a password or payment information. If the domain looks unfamiliar, close the page. Then open the service yourself through its official app or website. This same habit can protect you from fake banking sites. We recently covered criminals who bought sponsored search ads that sent victims to lookalike bank login pages.

Never reuse your ChatGPT password on other accounts. We recommend using a unique password and suggest a password manager to generate and store it. That way, one stolen password cannot easily unlock several of your accounts.

OpenAI supports two-factor authentication, or 2FA. You can enable it from the Security section of your ChatGPT settings. Depending on your account, available verification methods may include an authenticator app, push notification, text message or passkey. 2FA adds another hurdle if someone gets your password. However, enabling 2FA does not automatically end sessions that are already logged in.

Strong antivirus software can help warn you about malicious links and phishing websites. It can also block other threats that may arrive through scam emails. Keep that protection updated on every device where you check email or sign in to important accounts. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com

Change your password immediately if you entered it on a suspicious site. Then open ChatGPT and go to Settings → Security → Active sessions . Review the listed devices and sessions. If you see something you do not recognize, log it out.

OpenAI also lets you go to Settings → Security → Active sessions and choose Log out of all session s. The company says signing out across every device can take up to 30 minutes. If you use Google, Microsoft or Apple to sign in to ChatGPT, secure that account as well.

If you gave a suspicious site your card information, call the number on the back of the card. Tell the issuer that your payment information may have been compromised. Then review recent transactions for anything you do not recognize. Your card issuer may recommend replacing the card. Follow its instructions rather than waiting for a fraudulent charge to appear.

Cofense says the phishing campaign targeted people using ChatGPT through personal and work accounts. If you entered work credentials or used a company-managed account, contact your IT or security team. They can review account activity and take additional steps if necessary.

This scam works because the email looks like something you might actually expect to receive. A payment problem feels routine, and that can make people lower their guard. If you get a billing warning from ChatGPT, do not use the link in the message. Open ChatGPT yourself and check your account there. If you already entered your password on a suspicious page, change it right away and review your active sessions. If you shared payment information, contact your card issuer.

Have you ever received a subscription warning that looked completely legitimate, and what tipped you off before you clicked? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

item.title: SCOTUS detention fight could unleash dangerous criminal migrants onto US streets, experts warns
item.description: A Supreme Court battle over bond hearings for detained noncitizens with criminal records could make it harder for ICE to keep detainees locked up.
item.content:encoded:
A Supreme Court battle over whether certain noncitizens with criminal records are entitled to bond hearings during lengthy deportation proceedings could become a public safety concern by making it harder for the federal government to keep some detainees behind bars, legal experts warn.

The Trump administration is asking the justices to take up Genalo v. D.C., a case involving a Dominican citizen with four criminal convictions who has been detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement while fighting removal.

The dispute centers on a Second Circuit precedent requiring a bond hearing when mandatory immigration detention becomes "unreasonably prolonged." At that hearing, the government must prove by clear and convincing evidence that the detainee poses a flight risk or danger to the community.

MACHETE-WIELDING MS-13 GANGSTER WANTED FOR MURDER WALKS FREE AFTER BIDEN-APPOINTED JUDGE RELEASES HIM: DHS

Chad Mizelle, chair of litigation at the America First Policy Institute and a former acting associate attorney general and Justice Department chief of staff, told Fox News Digital the implications extend beyond immigration law.

"We are talking about criminal aliens here," Mizelle said. "Those are individuals who have been accused of or convicted of an aggravated felony. Accused or convicted of murder. Accused or convicted of child rape. Accused or convicted of grievous harm upon another human being."

"So these are the worst of the worst individuals," Mizelle continued. "Do we want those individuals walking the streets, re-committing, harming other individuals?"

Mizelle argued Congress imposed mandatory detention on certain noncitizens with criminal records to keep them detained during removal proceedings, while the Second Circuit’s prolonged-detention rule could incentivize some detainees to drag out their cases long enough to seek bond.

DOJ MOVES TO STRIP CITIZENSHIP FROM 17 PEOPLE ACCUSED OF HIDING DISTURBING CRIMES

The man at the center of the administration’s latest petition, identified in court papers as D.C., is a 62-year-old Dominican citizen who illegally entered the United States and has four criminal convictions, according to court records.

In 1997, D.C. was charged with multiple drug offenses, including selling and possessing a controlled substance. He failed to appear for trial, was convicted by a jury and sentenced in absentia to three to nine years in prison, but did not serve that sentence until 2024. In 2007, he was charged with possessing a forged instrument after presenting false identification to police and again failed to appear in court.

In 2016, D.C. faced several charges stemming from a domestic dispute, including second-degree strangulation, third-degree assault and acting in a manner to injure a child under 17. He pleaded guilty to criminal obstruction of breathing or blood circulation and also resolved his earlier forged-instrument case with a guilty plea. Later that year, he pleaded guilty to criminal contempt.

D.C. was finally arrested on the outstanding warrant from his 1998 drug conviction in April 2024. After completing his state sentence in September 2025, ICE immediately detained him while his removal proceedings continued.

FEDERAL APPEALS COURT COMPARES TRUMP MIGRANT DETENTION POLICY TO JAPANESE AMERICAN INTERNMENT

The district court subsequently ordered that D.C. receive a bond hearing under binding Second Circuit precedent but denied his separate request for immediate release. The government is now asking the Supreme Court to take the case before the Second Circuit itself rules — an unusual procedure known as certiorari before judgment.

The administration turned to D.C.’s case after two other noncitizens at the center of the same legal fight saw their cases become moot.

One, Carol Williams Black, had been detained for roughly seven months. His case became moot after he received a final order of removal and permanently left the United States. Black was convicted of sexually abusing a child in 2000. The Supreme Court therefore granted review in June only as to the second detainee, G.M.

G.M., a lawful permanent resident from the Dominican Republic, pleaded guilty to second-degree assault in May 2015 after being accused of attacking and robbing a man during a 2012 incident in New York City. He was sentenced to two years in prison and was released early on parole in December 2016 after serving 19 months. ICE arrested G.M. at his home on Oct. 5, 2020, and detained him for 21 months without a bond hearing while removal proceedings continued.

TRUMP’S FIGHT OVER RARELY USED 18TH-CENTURY DEPORTATION LAW LIVES ON IN LATEST COURT CLASH

The Supreme Court was scheduled to hear his case Oct. 13. But in late August, New York Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul granted G.M. a full and unconditional pardon for the assault conviction that had formed the basis for his deportation proceedings and mandatory detention. Solicitor General John Sauer agreed the case was moot, and the Supreme Court dismissed it Sept. 11 without ruling on the merits.

The administration then identified D.C. as its replacement vehicle and asked the justices to hear the same constitutional questions this term.

FEDERAL JUDGE TIES ICE AGENTS' HANDS WITH RULING ON WARRANTLESS SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA ARRESTS

Carrie Severino, president of Judicial Crisis Network (JCN), said the dispute is likely to affect many similar immigration cases nationwide.

"This is not a question that's only going to affect D.C., the criminal Dominican national at issue in this case," Severino told Fox News Digital. "This is an issue that's going to affect criminal aliens across the country."

A victory by D.C. would impose new hurdles on the government, including additional hearings and use of resources, Severino said.

"As we know, immigration cases, skipping out on showing up for court dates is incredibly common," she added. "This is not something that I think the court ought to be granting on a regular basis that they'd be letting people out on bond simply on their word that they're going to be coming back when they know that they are likely to be removed."

The case also raises questions about who must prove whether continued detention is necessary. The Second Circuit ruled that the government must prove by clear and convincing evidence that a detainee should remain in custody.

"And so, if the Supreme Court winds up affirming what the Second Circuit held, that means it's going to be harder for the government to be able to detain this particular population of criminal aliens or terrorism-linked aliens," Florida State University law professor Michael Morley told Fox News Digital. "There are going to be situations where the government is not able to show that a particular person is either likely to flee or poses a risk of danger and this dangerousness by a heightened or clear and convincing standard."

"It means that these criminal aliens who are already subject to removal proceedings are more likely to be released into the community while those underlying removal proceedings continue to make their way slowly through the adjudicative process," Morley continued.

The Supreme Court has not yet agreed to hear D.C.’s case.

item.title: Michigan man doxxed after exposing his city's booming Islamic surge takes defiant stand: 'Not gonna stop'
